forms.label: Vanilla
forms.animalOriginNote: Always dairy. Some vanilla ice cream is churned from an egg-yolk custard base (the French style) and some is egg-free (the Philadelphia style); which one a given tub is depends on the maker.
forms.sourceNote: Ice creams, vanilla. Public domain. No measured liquid density exists for this record, so the density-classes.json 'dairy-whole' class stands in and the figure is marked estimated — this is a real simplification, since commercial ice cream is churned with 30 to 50% air by volume that this figure cannot see, so it understates the space a weighed scoop actually occupies before it is blended smooth.
